    How to set up surround sound with Apple TV 4K and HomePods

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Surround yourself with Apple’s premium home theater experience — for a price.
    • The new Apple TV 4K (4th generation) has been generating buzz ever since it was declared at the Cupertino company's Welcome Home Event in October 2026.
    • To set up your home theater's surround sound system, you will need the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K and up to four 2nd generation HomePods or HomePod mini 2s.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Surround yourself with Apple’s premium home theater experience — for a price.

    The new Apple TV 4K (4th generation) has been generating buzz ever since it was declared at the Cupertino company's Welcome Home Event in October 2026. One of the most noteworthy changes is to its surround sound capabilities, in which owners can create an immersive cinematic experience in their own living room. Unfortunately, while many of the 4th generation's new features will be available for previous models, including its enhanced Siri AI system, Apple's venture into surround sound is not backwards compatible.

    To set up your home theater's surround sound system, you will need the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K and up to four 2nd generation HomePods or HomePod mini 2s. Apple's support page also states that you can pair two sets of either home speaker, but the front pair and rear pair must match (two HomePods and two HomePod mini 2s). Before setting up your system, update your devices to the most recent software. If you only have two speakers, either the HomePod or HomePod mini 2, you can still use them to create a home stereo setup.

    Sources indicate that those wanting to create this home theater setup from scratch will have to pay a pretty penny to do so. Officially released on November 13, 2026, you can purchase the 4th generation Apple TV 4K on Apple's website or at your local Apple Store for a hefty $299. But true sticker shock may set in when one considers the cost of four smart speakers, with the HomePod (2nd generation) and HomePod mini 2 costing $349 and $149, respectively. All told, that could cost you up to $1,700 for Apple's most advanced audio experience. Whether the system's various AI and quality updates help soften the blow is up to you.

    The first thing you should do is assign your Apple TV 4K and HomePod speakers to the same room in the Home app. To assign your Apple TV 4K to a room, turn on your Apple TV and open the Settings app. Next, select AirPlay and Apple Home, navigate to the Select a Room option beneath Apple Home and assign your Apple TV accordingly.

    Next, you need to assign your speaker system. To add your HomePod (2nd generation) or HomePod mini 2, turn on your speaker and open the Home app on your iPhone or iPad. Tap the Add button and select Add Accessory. You will be prompted to scan a code or hold your device near the speaker. When it appears, tap the speaker name and tap Allow when prompted to Add Accessory to Network. Finally, choose the same room as your Apple TV 4K, name it, tap Continue > Done. Repeat this process for all four speakers.

    You can change the room of an existing HomePod in the Home app on your iPhone or iPad. Simply open the Home application and hold your finger down on the HomePod whose location you would like to change. Next, select the Accessories Settings button with the gear symbol. Press the Room tab and select the room of your home theater. You can also add a latest room in this page by tapping Create New. Once you have added all your devices to the same room, you are ready to set up surround sound.

    Now, it's time to set up your surround sound configuration. Go to your Home app, tap a HomePod and select the gear icon at the bottom. Then, scroll until you find the Create Home Theater option and tap the HomePods that you want to group into your home theater system. Once grouped, tap the checkmark at the top corner. You should now see a notification instructing you to continue the set up process on your Apple TV.

    Next, turn on your Apple TV. Follow the onscreen prompts instructing you on where to place your speakers. If using a combination of HomePods and HomPod mini 2 speakers, Apple suggests that you place the larger speakers at the front of the room. Once in place, select Start Tuning. Your home theater will now begin tuning to your space by playing a series of tones. Once finished, follow the on screen instructions confirming your speaker's placements and color selections before hitting Confirm. Now you are ready for an immersive home theater experience.

    According to recent reports, if you'd rather create a stereo system using two Apple smart speakers, visit to your Home app, select your HomePod, and tap Settings. Next, tap Create Stereo Pair and follow the onscreen instructions. From there, follow the steps above to assign your stereo to the same room as your Apple TV 4K. Once finished, turn your Apple TV on and follow the onscreen prompts until you are prompted to Use as TV Speakers.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to conduct computer work on behalf of users — including using apps, accessing websites, and coding, among other things.

    The news was originally reported by Bloomberg, which spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an “AI agent that can use a computer.”.

    Sources indicate that “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the posting notes. “It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.”.

    The posting additionally notes that the agents should be able to move “fluidly between tools” and “carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.”.

    TechCrunch reached out to Apple for more information but did not receive a response.

    In a recent development, agents capable of computer work have become one of the hottest commodities in the tech industry over the past year. Major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI have rolled out such services, while other major tech brands — like Meta, which recently launched its Muse agent line — have also moved into the space. It makes sense that Apple — which is trying to expand its AI offerings in the new John Ternus era — would want to follow suit.

    Bloomberg additionally notes that, at the same time that Apple is working on its own digital assistant, the manufacturer is making it significantly harder for third-party agents to gain total control over its computers.

    In a recent development, the outlet notes that the version of its upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging users from granting full access to third-party agents. In October, Apple issued a notification to developers stating that the manufacturer planned to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”.

    Bloomberg writes that while the iPhone maker “has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year,” progress on its in-house agent “remains in the early stages.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Watch: Inside court as Nikhil Gupta sentenced to 19 years over assassination plot.

    A federal judge sentenced an Indian man to 235 months, more than 19 years, in an attempted plot to kill a leading Sikh political figure in the US.

    Nikhil Gupta, an Indian national, pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering in February. On Friday, the judge stated he likely will be deported or removed after his sentence.

    US prosecutors alleged Gupta was directed by an Indian government official to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a leading figure of the Khalistan movement, which advocates for an independent homeland for Sikhs.

    India has denied involvement. Its government has accused Pannun of being a terrorist, which he denies.

    Pannun, an American citizen, is the spokesman for US-based Sikh separatist group Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), banned in India since 2019.

    He previously told the BBC that "Nikhil Gupta's guilty plea was judicial confirmation that India's Modi government orchestrated a structured murder-for-hire assassination plot on American soil".

    India has opposed the Khalistan movement, and its political parties also remain opposed to the matter. Sikhs are a religious minority that make up about 2% of India's population. Some groups have long called for a separate homeland for Sikhs.

    In a recent development, nikhil Gupta (seen in a 2024 courtroom sketch) pleaded guilty in a plot to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a U.S. resident who advocated for a sovereign Sikh state in northern India.

    Prosecutors alleged that in May 2023, Gupta was recruited by Vikash Yadav, an Indian intelligence officer, to carry out an assassination of Pannun.

    Yadav allegedly provided Gupta with personal information about Pannun, including his address in Newly introduced York and information about his daily activities, prosecutors said.

    Sources indicate that at his handler's direction, Gupta contacted someone to facilitate the assassination, but that person was actually a US government informant, prosecutors said. The informant introduced Gupta to a "hitman", who was actually an undercover officer with the Drug Enforcement Agency.

    Gupta was arrested in June 2023 at an airport in Prague, Czech Republic and extradited to the US. He has been held at a jail in Newly introduced York pending his sentencing Friday at a Manhattan court.

    "He thought that from outside this country he could kill someone in it without consequence, simply for exercising their American right to free speech," then-US attorney Jay Clayton mentioned in a statement, after announcing Gupta's guilty plea.

    Following Gupta's arrest, a spokesperson for India's Ministry of External Affairs noted that Yadav is no longer employed, external by the Indian government.

    The country also set up an inquiry committee to address security concerns raised by the US, the spokesperson stated.

    Narinder Singh Randhawa, a Sikh separatist and successor of Hardeep Singh Nijjar as temple leader in Surrey, British Columbia, told the BBC the sentencing marks the "first time we see justice" against what he calls historic and systemic persecution of Sikhs by the Indian government in India and abroad.

    Inderjeet Gosal, another Sikh separatist advocate based in Ontario, called the sentencing "a big community event".

    "It's for all the community to finally witness someone getting caught red-handed.".

    Indian man admits plot to kill US-based Sikh separatist leader.

    Who was Canadian Sikh leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar?

    Canada accuses India of role in Sikh leader's murder.

    India crushed a violent armed Sikh insurgency in the 1980s and 1990s aimed at demanding the creation of Khalistan. The movement has little support in India now although some in the Sikh diaspora continue to advocate for Khalistan.

    Pannun is facing serious charges, including in connection with terrorism, in India, but he denies the allegations, saying he is an activist who just believes in Khalistan.

    In a victim impact statement to the court, Pannun said the foiled assassination attempt has not deterred his activism.

    "I am entirely willing to take India's bullets if that is the price required to achieve freedom," he wrote.

    Gupta's case placed increased scrutiny on a separate incident, involving the 2023 murder of a Sikh separatist leader in British Columbia, which led to increased tensions between India and Canada.

    In September 2023, then-Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau noted there were "credible allegations potentially linking" India to the murder of Hardeep Singh Nijjar, another advocate for the creation of Khalistan and an associate of Pannun's.

    It has been revealed that nijjar was shot and killed by two assailants outside a Sikh temple in British Columbia. India also has denied involvement in his death.

    The day after Niijar's murder, US prosecutors allege that Gupta told the undercover officer Nijjar "was also the target" and "we have so many targets.".

    #35895. This retro classic is the most re-released game of all time — here's why

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1152 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    This retro classic is the most re-released game of all time — here's why

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1152 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The most re-released game is also one of the best-selling, and it’s not even close.
    • You might initially think the most re-released game of all time is something like Skyrim, which is notorious for its various editions.
    • Industry observers note that but another classic game dwarfs the appearances of any other: Tetris.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The most re-released game is also one of the best-selling, and it’s not even close.

    You might initially think the most re-released game of all time is something like Skyrim, which is notorious for its various editions. Or you may instead point to the original Super Mario Bros., which has appeared on almost every Nintendo console in some form, or Sonic the Hedgehog for its inclusion in tons of compilations.

    Industry observers note that but another classic game dwarfs the appearances of any other: Tetris. Following its initial development on a Soviet computer, this renowned puzzler quickly spread around the world and appeared on virtually every platform you can imagine. With over 200 official releases, alongside countless ports and bootleg versions, there's been a version of Tetris to play no matter what device you have around.

    As you may know, the legacy of Tetris started in the Soviet Union in 1984-1985, when programmer Alexey Pajitnov developed games for fun. He first built the game for the Soviet Elektronika 60 computer, using text-based graphics ([] characters for the tetrominoes) since that machine didn't have graphical output.

    After its inception, Pajitnov and a few colleagues worked to port the game to the incredibly popular IBM PC before making it known around the region by passing out copies. Pajitnov's manager liked the game and was one of the first who worked to distribute it to other parts of the world. In the following years, versions were created for popular computers at the time, such as the Commodore 64, Amiga and Mac.

    Arguably the most important version of Tetris was its release on Game Boy in 1989. Nintendo executives went through a long process, including a legal battle, to license the game for its upcoming handheld. They were ultimately successful in securing the rights, which led to Tetris coming bundled with the console in every market except Japan. This release was the first to have the iconic "Theme A" music; Pajitnov has remarked it's his favorite version, and it's by far the best-seller (not including mobile versions) with more than 35 million copies sold.

    Industry observers note that in 1996, Alexey Pajitnov created The Tetris Organization with longtime business partner Henk Rogers (who played a huge part in spreading Tetris around the world) to manage future branding and licensing. Since then, the game has been modified, re-released and ported (officially and unofficially) like crazy. There was even a Tetris movie on Apple TV, released in 2023.

    It has been revealed that anyone who has played Tetris in any form will understand how addictive its gameplay is. The concept of clearing horizontal lines only takes a moment to understand, and then you can spend a lifetime getting better at it. You only need a few buttons to move and rotate blocks, which, combined with the simple graphics, means Tetris can appear on almost any device, including unofficial ports to unexpected platforms like graphing calculators. Its bundling with the wildly successful Game Boy meant tons of people were exposed to it early on and thus have nostalgia for the game.

    According to recent reports, as we saw with the various releases above, Tetris also hasn't been stagnant. The Tetris Tech giant has internal rules known as the Tetris Guideline, which dictate how official releases should play, look and be controlled.

    Tetris's popularity has even led to other puzzle games using the name for marketing. The SNES game known as Tetris Attack was called Panel de Pon in its original Japanese release, but Nintendo licensed the Tetris name for other markets, assuming people would associate the title with block games in general. Nintendo used the name Puzzle League for later releases outside Japan.

    Many people consider Tetris to be a perfect game; its enduring legacy and "easy to learn, tough to master" gameplay definitely put it in the running for one of the best ever.

    It's not feasible to discuss every version of Tetris, but it's interesting to look at some of the most notable iterations. The NES release, which also debuted in 1989, is unique because it wasn't intended to be played indefinitely like most other versions. Instead, the game speeds up drastically past a certain point, which was designed to be a run's natural ending. This initially led to competition centering around racking up a max score before the "kill screen," but in recent years, players have developed techniques to play past the point that was previously thought impossible.

    NES Tetris also makes for a good competition version because it's more "hardcore." It lacks quality-of-life features present in later releases, like holding a piece, plus there's no grace period for movement once a tetromino touches the bottom — it's locked in instantly. And unlike later games that have a pseudo-random system to make sure you get each tetromino shape every so often, NES Tetris can have droughts where you never see the I-block you need.

    The Game Boy Color got Tetris DX in 1998, which updated the Game Boy release with color. It was the first version to offer the now-staple Sprint mode, where you race to clear 40 lines instead of the typical endless gameplay. The New Tetris, released on Nintendo 64 in 1999, was the first mainstream version to allow four players to compete simultaneously. It also marked the introduction of the ability to hold a piece to swap in later.

    Tetris DS (2006) is beloved for featuring multiple modes, each themed in the style of Nintendo franchises like Zelda and Metroid. It's regularly cited as one of the best releases and was the first official Tetris game to feature online play.

    Industry observers note that skipping forward a bit, Puyo Puyo Tetris is a fun mix of two classic puzzle series. Puyo Puyo is substantial in Japan but rarely received releases in other regions before this, with most of them being reskins under other franchises like Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine and Kirby's Avalanche. After its Japanese release in 2014, Puyo Puyo Tetris arrived in other regions in early 2017, with various modes that mash up the two play styles.

    It has been revealed that 2018's Tetris Effect is the most beautiful version of the concept. It takes you on a "journey" through various visual landscapes, with lovely background music to immerse you in the experience. You also have the ability to stop time and clear more than four lines at once. It was initially limited to VR platforms, but an expanded version called Tetris Effect: Connected brought it to all modern systems in standard view. Meanwhile, in 2019, Tetris 99 adapted the battle royale craze to the puzzle game, pitting you against 98 people and rewarding you for knocking others out by sending garbage to their boards.

    Most recently, 2024's Tetris Forever serves as an interactive museum of the series after 40 years, including interviews and various playable versions.

    #35894. Breaking: NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some substantial questions remain

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some substantial questions remain

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2312 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SpaceX’s successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA’s path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-crucial, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year.
    • Recent findings suggest that for SpaceX’s purposes, Saturday’s mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships.
    • Recent findings suggest that early next year, SpaceX prepares to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SpaceX’s successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA’s path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-crucial, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year.

    Recent findings suggest that for SpaceX’s purposes, Saturday’s mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships. That should expedite SpaceX’s deployment of its newest generation of Starlink Internet satellites. NASA, meanwhile, believes a higher launch cadence will lead to faster learning as SpaceX develops a deep space version of Starship to ferry astronaut crews to the surface of the Moon.

    Recent findings suggest that early next year, SpaceX prepares to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida. A second Starship factory is also under construction at Kennedy, joining SpaceX’s existing SpaceX production line at Starbase, Texas. With two launch sites, SpaceX will have the pieces in place to take the next leap with Starship.

    The Starship refueling demonstration has slipped two years since late 2024, effectively a day-for-day delay as SpaceX ironed out technical problems with the vehicle. SpaceX may have turned a corner with Saturday’s first-ever catch of Starship at the launch tower.

    According to recent reports, other Starship lander tests are coming next year. The first will be NASA’s Artemis III mission, followed by an uncrewed Starship landing demonstration on the Moon. The former requires no orbital refueling, and the latter will need heaps of it.

    Ars recently spoke with Steve Creech, the program manager for NASA’s Human Landing System. In this role, Creech oversees NASA’s contracts with SpaceX and Blue Origin to develop crew-rated lunar landers for Artemis.

    Sources indicate that for Artemis III, NASA will launch a four-person crew to low-Earth orbit on a Space Launch System rocket and an Orion spacecraft. Orion will first dock with Blue Origin’s Blue Moon lander for two days of tests, following its launch on a Fresh Glenn rocket. The astronauts will open hatches and enter Blue Moon’s pressurized crew cabin to test the vehicle’s environmental control and life support systems.

    Then, the astronauts will return to Orion and undock from Blue Moon to set up for a rendezvous and docking with SpaceX’s Starship in a slightly lower orbit, keeping it below most of SpaceX’s Starlink constellation. Orion will stay attached to Starship for just two hours, and the astronauts won’t enter the SpaceX vehicle.

    Industry observers note that NASA changed the plan for the Artemis III mission earlier this year, rerouting the flight plan from a lunar mission to a low-Earth orbit mission. This means the Artemis program’s first crewed lunar landing will be on Artemis IV, targeted to launch before the end of 2028.

    In a recent development, so, why is Artemis III seemingly testing so much more with Blue Origin than with Starship? Creech told Ars that a big reason is to maintain SpaceX’s focus on orbital refueling. Blue Origin no longer requires in-space refueling for Artemis landing missions. Also, SpaceX has extensive experience with life support systems with its Dragon crewed spacecraft. Blue Origin has comparatively little.

    Recent findings suggest that “The bigger challenges for [SpaceX] were the prop transfer and getting to the uncrewed landing demo,” Creech stated. “The thing that we’re going to learn more with Starship is, when we dock with Orion, they will have control of the attitude, control of the stack. That integrated stack control will be on the Starship side. So, with that huge of a vehicle, I think we’re going to learn more on that.

    Recent findings suggest that “With Blue, we’re going to have Orion control the stack for this mission,” Creech said. “When we get to a later mission, the Blue lander with fully loaded prop will have to control the stack. But with Blue, trying to mitigate risk, we’re going to have Orion do that.”.

    Artemis III will be Blue Origin’s first time flying a crew cabin for orbital spaceflight. Blue Origin has experience with suborbital space tourism, but those flights were brief and didn’t require the level of advanced life support necessary for longer durations. Blue Origin and NASA will emphasize those test objectives on Artemis III.

    In a recent development, “I think SpaceX’s part was really, we need to focus on the docking,” Creech mentioned. “If we added a crew cabin, that would slow us down on the other things and not add to what we’re already doing.”.

    It has been revealed that the Starship on Artemis III will have a full complement of Raptor engines and a docking port on its nose. Blue Moon will not have any main engines when it links up with Orion on Artemis III, only a set of smaller thrusters for pointing control and minor maneuvers.

    It has been revealed that “With Blue, you don’t have a BE-7 engine, you don’t have the cryo tanks,” Creech stated. “They’re representing the mass of the lander when it comes back from the surface because we think that’s the most critical case. But it does have the crew cabin.”.

    Recent findings suggest that while there’s no Starship life support demonstration on Artemis III, NASA added a fresh milestone to SpaceX’s Moon lander contract to test parts of its crew cabin on the ground. The additional testing involves construction of a prototype crew compartment, called Cabin One, at SpaceX’s test site at Starbase, Texas.

    Sources indicate that NASA levied new test requirements on Blue Origin, too. The organization prepares to launch its first Blue Moon test mission early next year after a monthslong delay caused by a rocket explosion on Blue Origin’s launch pad in May. This version of Blue Moon, known as Mark 1, has a single hydrogen-fueled BE-7 main engine. Future human-rated landers from Blue Origin will have three.

    “One of the things we added into the program in the last year is, we really felt like we needed a test of the three-engine configuration,” Creech mentioned. The hotfire test of the three-engine Blue Moon propulsion unit will occur inside a vacuum chamber at NASA’s In-Space Propulsion Facility in Ohio.

    This year’s Artemis shakeup did more than change the flight plan for Artemis III. Engineers also altered the architecture for subsequent lunar landing missions. The updated plans will make life easier for teams working on Starship and Blue Moon. That’s not necessarily the case for Orion.

    It has been revealed that “Our previous architecture for both these landers required a 90-day loiter in lunar orbit for Orion to arrive,” Creech noted. “That was something that, for both of these landers, drove a lot of complexity, and a lot of it made the lander job really hard.”.

    The latest concept of operations removes some of that complexity, according to NASA.

    “One of the things we changed was that 90-day loiter,” Creech said. “SpaceX, they solved it by saying let’s do an Earth orbit rendezvous with Orion, and take Orion to the Moon. For both Blue Origin and SpaceX, we have updated their requirements to a four-day surface day initially. Before, our initial missions were six-and-a-half days.”.

    Industry observers note that the six-and-a-half-day surface stay was baked into the Artemis architecture because the Orion spacecraft was originally planned to settle into a long, looping path around the Moon, called a near-rectilinear halo orbit. This orbit was predicated by the expected location of NASA’s now-canceled Gateway lunar space station. That, in turn, was driven by Orion’s inability to reach an orbit closer to the Moon.

    Now, instead of rendezvousing with Starship near the Moon on landing missions, Orion will link up with Starship in high-Earth orbit. From there, Starship will propel it toward the Moon.

    What’s still unclear, however, is whether SpaceX will have to refuel Starship at an altitude above low-Earth orbit. A graphic presented by Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager, last month illustrated this possibility with a “final tanking orbit” before Starship docks with Orion in high-Earth orbit.

    “We’re still working that out,” Creech remarked. “We’re making progress, but where we actually rendezvous with Orion is still in trade, so that’s why you saw a little bit of fuzziness there.”.

    According to recent reports, for missions using Blue Moon, the lander will connect with Orion in orbit around the Moon. Blue Origin’s updated looks do away with the requirement for in-space refueling but will still require four rolls out of the organization’s New Glenn rocket, one for the Blue Moon lander itself and three with transfer stages to boost it out of Earth orbit to the Moon.

    In a recent development, A latest stretched Centaur upper stage for the Space Launch System should give the rocket energy to send Orion to low-lunar orbit, which it could not reach with the current version of SLS. NASA has not determined if the new Centaur exploration stage will be ready in time for Artemis IV. If not, Artemis IV could fly with the last of NASA’s in-stock SLS upper stages.

    It has been revealed that NASA is also waiting to decide which lander to use on Artemis IV. In either case, two of Orion’s four astronauts will transfer into the landers for the final descent to the lunar surface for a four-day stay, then take off and return to Orion.

    Starship and Blue Moon must each complete an uncrewed landing demonstration before a crewed lunar mission. The landing demos are targeted for late 2027 or early 2028, Creech said, but they won’t necessarily test everything crews will need when they head for the lunar south pole.

    Recent findings suggest that starship’s elevator, for example, is not part of SpaceX’s uncrewed landing demonstration. Engineers will use a test lab at Marshall Space Flight Center in Alabama to check the elevator’s performance in a simulated lunar environment.

    NASA did not initially require SpaceX or Blue Origin to prove their landers could take off from the Moon before a crew mission. Government officials later added the lunar takeoff requirement for each organization’s uncrewed landing demos.

    For now, NASA is leaving the details of the uncrewed takeoff demo up to SpaceX and Blue Origin. During Apollo, NASA’s lunar lander never landed on the Moon before Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin descended to the Sea of Tranquility. NASA did, however, fly a dress rehearsal around the Moon on Apollo 10 that included a test of the lunar module’s landing abort capability.

    “Where we are today is, Blue will land and then do a full ascent back to the rendezvous point with Orion,” Creech remarked. “With SpaceX. They will land, they will take off again, get to main stage on the engines, and then they will do another landing on the surface.”.

    That could change. Today’s plan gives SpaceX two shots at proving Starship can safely land on the Moon, but it comes with trade-offs.

    Sources indicate that “When I came into the program, I was like, ‘Why are we not going all the way to the rendezvous point?’” stated Creech, who took over as HLS program manager in 2025. “Some of my key people felt strongly we would get more out of the way we’re doing it now. There are others that have different opinions… We tend to have a lot of technical discussion and debate. That point will continue to be debated.”.

    For Starship, orbital refueling remains the key to the Moon. SpaceX’s propellant transfer demonstration will involve two Starships, one debuted from Florida and another from Texas, docking together in low-Earth orbit and transferring a “meaningful” amount of propellant from one ship to the other, Creech noted.

    It has been revealed that “The first quarter of next year, we will see a long-awaited propellant transfer test from SpaceX, where they launch two Starships in pretty close proximity, actually dock, and transfer, we’re calling it a meaningful amount, of propellant,” Creech told Ars. “That is going to be a significant learning point if they pull that off, because their architecture depends on propellant aggregation and multiple propellant flights.”.

    The propellant transfer test will mark the first time one spacecraft has offloaded a significant quantity of cryogenic propellants—in this case, methane and liquid oxygen—onto another vehicle in space. It is the culmination of decades of government and commercial research on cryogenic orbital refueling. The results will tell engineers how much of the propellant will be lost from boil-off during the transfer.

    Sources indicate that that is one reason why there’s still so much ambiguity about how many Starship refueling tankers SpaceX will need to launch to give the Starship lunar lander enough gas to fly to the Moon. Without refueling, Starships are restricted to flights in low-Earth orbit.

    According to recent reports, the low end of the estimate for Starship tankers is six to eight refueling flights to support a Starship lunar mission. Those numbers come from Elon Musk, SpaceX’s founder and CEO, and fall below NASA’s own conservative planning figure of 20 refueling debuts. Musk’s figures hinge on future Starship upgrades to reach the vehicle’s full potential. SpaceX’s goal is to get Starship’s lift capacity up to 100 to 200 metric tons of payload to low-Earth orbit. Today’s version of Starship, known as Starship V3, is still far short of 100 metric tons of payload capacity.

    Industry observers note that for context, a Starship carries 1,600 metric tons of propellant with its tanks full. Refueling flights using future, fully optimized Starships might be able to fill those tanks with as few as six tankers. That is not the case today.

    SpaceX is working on a taller, heavier Starship called Starship V4. It will fly with nine Raptor engines, an upgrade over the six-engine variant flying today. In 2025, Musk mentioned Starship V4’s first launch was targeted for 2027. There hasn’t been a recent upgrade to the schedule for Starship V4.

    The initial Artemis lunar missions will use Starship V3, Creech mentioned.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    In a recent development, white House national cyber director Sean Cairncross will be stepping down from his role, Axios reported. The news comes as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress and as businesses across the country report a flurry of technical outages whose cause remains unknown.

    It has been revealed that cairncross, the president’s principal adviser on national cybersecurity policy and strategy, took office in August 2025. Since then, he has met with top AI leaders and helped the Trump administration make key AI decisions, according to Axios. The outlet also reports that the split between Cairncross and the White House was amicable, and his departure was timed so that the White House could nab a Senate confirmation for his role before Democrats take control of Congress in January.

    In a recent development, cairncross, a lawyer and longtime Republican operative, had no cybersecurity background when the Senate confirmed him 59–35. He previously served as the Republican National Committee’s chief operating officer and, during Trump’s first term, as CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation, a federal foreign aid agency. The office hasn’t been around long; Congress created it in early 2021, and Cairncross was only its third Senate-confirmed director. The first director, Chris Inglis, left after about 19 months, and the job then went about 10 months without a permanent director.

    We’ve reached out to the White House for comment.

    California investigates Nvidia over whether chip exports ended up in China

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • State attorney notes scandal ‘raises bright red flags’ and aims to find out if tech giant misled investors.
    • California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang.
    • Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based company’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    State attorney notes scandal ‘raises bright red flags’ and aims to find out if tech giant misled investors.

    California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang.

    Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based company’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions.

    “The conduct of Nvidia and its former chief executive raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the firm may have misled investors,” said Bonta.

    “Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: companies cannot mislead their investors.”.

    The subpoena, issued on Thursday, followed Huang’s resignation a week ago after it emerged he had multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy.

    Alice Huang, who is not related, is associated with Singapore-based Megaspeed, which has bought nearly $5bn (£3.8bn) of Nvidia chips and hardware in recent years, and is being investigated for possibly diverting advanced restricted chips to China.

    Megaspeed has stated it is a “legitimate and lawful” business, and that Huang left the manufacturer late last year.

    Bonta stated the investigation would also look at whether the former Nvidia chief’s actions resulted in confidential information being passed to China.

    “My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang’s actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information,” he stated. “And if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law.”.

    Nvidia’s shares are down by a fifth since Huang admitted the extramarital affair, hitting a one-year low at the close of trading on Thursday, and wiping almost $1tn off its market value.

    Recent findings suggest that earlier this week, Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s chair, stated the tech giant had no intention of reinstating Huang after the former CEO said he would be “honoured” to return. Elon Musk and a host of tech bosses had campaigned for Nvidia to bring him back.

    Huang is due to testify before several congressional committees over the potential breach of national security on 1 December.

    Shares in rival chipmaker AMD closed down almost 8% on Thursday after the publication of reports connected to short seller Hunterbrook warning about its links to China and the “circular financing” of customers.

    The company, which has been targeted amid the Nvidia scandal, is looking at a further fall of more than 5% in pre-market trading.

    Hunterbrook Media published allegations on the use of AMD’s software by a Chinese server maker blacklisted by the US. Sister publication, The Bear Cave newsletter, alleged that AMD’s use of datacentre lease guarantees and backstops for unsold cloud computing capacity could leave it exposed to a pullback in AI spending.

    AMD said the reports’ claims “misrepresent AMD’s business practices and relationships”.

    “AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations,” the company stated. “We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.”.

    AMD’s share price has more than doubled so far this year, giving the company a market capitalisation of more than $800m.

    Industry News: HomeView vs. Echo Show: What's the difference between Apple's and Amazon's smart displays?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Both put an AI assistant in your home, but they work in different ways.
    • In a recent development, amazon and Google have long been the top choices when it comes to smart displays, but Apple has now joined the race with HomeView.
    • The differences start with size: While the HomeView is a new product and is available in a single version with a 7-inch square screen, Amazon offers a range of Echo Show devices with different screen sizes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Both put an AI assistant in your home, but they work in different ways.

    In a recent development, amazon and Google have long been the top choices when it comes to smart displays, but Apple has now joined the race with HomeView. For $299, Apple offers a touchscreen and built-in speakers with an experience optimized for those deeply immersed in the tech giant's ecosystem — it includes Messages, Apple Music and, of course, built-in HomeKit. It's impossible not to compare it to Amazon's Echo Show, which recently added a new 16-inch model to its lineup. But even though both are smart displays, they work in very different ways — and choosing between them ultimately comes down to which ecosystem you have at home.

    The differences start with size: While the HomeView is a new product and is available in a single version with a 7-inch square screen, Amazon offers a range of Echo Show devices with different screen sizes. The entry-level Echo Show has a 5.5-inch screen and costs $99 — but if you want to go bigger, there's even an Echo Show with a massive 21-inch screen for $499. They all share mostly the same features, although the 16-inch and 21-inch models can run Fire TV apps.

    It has been revealed that amazon's Echo Show 8 is the one that can be easily compared to HomeView, with an 8.7-inch display. The aspect ratio is different, though, as Echo devices have widescreen displays and are better for watching 16:9 videos. The HomeView's square shape might annoy those planning to buy one to watch videos on it. Also on Apple's side, HomeView runs on the same A18 chip as the iPhone 16 — which probably makes it the most powerful smart display available. Amazon, on the other hand, makes custom chips for its Echo devices that aren't exactly designed to deliver Earth-shattering performance.

    Recent findings suggest that both the HomeView and the Echo Show 8 have a built-in camera, but the software makes them work quite differently. The HomeView's 12-megapixel camera only works with FaceTime and a Mirror feature, and, of course, for facial recognition. With the Echo Show 8, you can take selfies with its 13-megapixel camera it or use it as a live-view camera to monitor your home. The sound specs are quite similar between the two of them, as both have two full-range drivers and a woofer. The HomeView's base also packs two passive radiators for a bit more low end.

    According to recent reports, the biggest difference between the HomeView and Amazon devices is how they work. While the Echo Show is a standalone device linked to an Amazon account that can run directly on your network, the HomeView requires an iPhone or iPad to work — you can't set it up without one. On Echo Show devices, you can also use Alexa+ through your Prime membership to manage calendars, reminders and shopping without your phone. The HomeView comes with Siri AI built-in, but it can only handle personal requests if you have a recently unlocked iPhone 15 Pro or later paired with it and nearby.

    It has been revealed that both the Echo Show and HomeView devices can have multiple profiles verified by voice and facial recognition. However, while Amazon lets users manually switch between profiles by asking Alexa, for example, HomeView does it all automatically — which, according to some early reviews, doesn't always work.

    The truth is, both products target different consumers. Amazon treats the Echo Show as a standalone product that fits almost everyone. The HomeView is a different story — it's much more like an accessory for people who already own other Apple products and rely on the organization's core apps and features.

    Industry News: Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," said Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU).
    • The government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world.
    • To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," said Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU). Recently adopted by the Cabinet, the government's fourth report on the subject covers developments from 2023 to 2025.

    The government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world. According to the report, this freedom is facing "increasing pressure" globally. The focus is not primarily on the suppression of religious institutions or structures, but on the situation of individuals who hold a religious belief, or none at all.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    The importance of religious freedom is reflected in the way the government commissioner describes the issue: "Religion and faith are of great importance to four out of five people around the world and are central to their identity. People wake up with God and go to sleep with God. It is part of their everyday lives." Research by the Pew Research Center suggests that about 84% of the world's population identifies with a certain religion.

    It has been revealed that at a time when authoritarian regimes are gaining ground and expanding their surveillance capabilities, the report paints a bleak picture. The growing number of violent conflicts, the rise of authoritarian rule, and the spread of populism have led to "painful restrictions on freedom of religion and belief around the world.".

    The German government report does not attempt to provide a statistical tally of attacks or the number of people facing persecution. Instead, it examines 30 countries as case studies where, in the federal government's view, freedom of religion and belief is being restricted. These include about six countries each from Africa, Asia, and the Arab world. In Europe, the report focuses on Belarus, Russia, Ukraine, and Turkey, while in Latin America it highlights Mexico, Nicaragua, and Cuba. It also identifies shortcomings in five of the world's six most populous countries: China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Nigeria.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Industry observers note that regarding India, the report refers to "Hindu nationalist efforts" that threaten the equal treatment of all officially recognized religions. It states that the generally peaceful coexistence of different faiths is "repeatedly overshadowed by tensions and, at times, violence." Both Muslim and Christian communities report growing intolerance and hate speech. According to the report, violent Hindu extremist groups have carried out a "large number of physical attacks" against Muslims, while the police and government authorities often respond inadequately.

    In China, the German government identifies a "significant tightening of the legal framework of state control at the expense of freedom of religion and belief." According to the report, this particularly affects Uyghurs, Tibetans and churches that lack official state approval and are subject to harsh measures by the authorities. The law on the "Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress," which came into force on July 1, 2026, subordinates religion to "the formation of national identity" and patriotic education.

    One of the countries where the situation has deteriorated most dramatically is Nicaragua, which has severely restricted freedom of religion and belief since 2018. The repression has primarily targeted the Catholic Church. According to the report, "intimidation, persecution, imprisonment, and expulsion" have forced around 130 priests and nuns to leave the country.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    It has been revealed that the reports reserves some of its sharpest criticism for Kirill, the patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church. Under his leadership, the church has strongly supported Russia's war against Ukraine and portrayed it as a "holy war." According to the report, "weapons are blessed, Russian soldiers are absolved of their sins, and donations are collected for the war." It is perhaps the clearest example in the report of how religion can be used to justify oppression and violence.

    Sources indicate that the report explicitly addresses the threat posed by "transnational repression" (TNR), which it describes as a "growing global problem" that also affects Germany. The term refers to the persecution or intimidation of individuals by their country of origin beyond its own borders.

    Ultimately, it argues, this amounts to a "continuation of domestic repression." Such "cross-border repression" has become considerably easier through the growing availability of digital means of repression, including smear campaigns on social media and spyware.

    According to recent reports, these forms of pressure range from physical attacks on individuals to digital assaults such as online intimidation and defamation. In some cases, repression is also carried out by threatening family members who remain in the country of origin. Russia and Iran, for example, are identified as the "main perpetrators of transnational repression" in Germany.

    It has been revealed that china is a particularly prominent example of religious and ideological tensions. Repression by Beijing in Germany primarily targets members of groups that the country's Communist Party classifies as "hostile to the system." These include Uyghurs, Tibetans, and members of the Falun Gong movement. According to the report, they are "also subject to surveillance and repressive measures in Germany," while relatives living in China are pressured.

    Thomas Rachel hopes the newly published report will be "discussed in as many Bundestag committees as possible" and that members of parliament will "engage with the issue accordingly." Previous government reports on the subject have been debated in the Bundestag plenary at least once and, in some cases, twice.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    The problem's place within the German government has also changed during the current legislative term. Commissioner Thomas Rachel is now based at the Foreign Ministry, while both of his predecessors since 2018 were attached to the Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development. Today, Rachel claims, the importance of religion is being "taken into account" in German foreign policy. He also points to his involvement in the Foreign Ministry's diplomatic training programs.

    Industry observers note that in doing so, the government led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) reversed a structural decision made by the previous center-left coalition, which was led from 2021 to 2025 by Chancellor Olaf Scholz of the Social Democratic Party (SPD). The Scholz government had reduced the issue's prominence by assigning it to the "Religion and Foreign Policy" division. Religion and foreign policy have now regained a more prominent place within government.

    Sources indicate that one example is the current foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, who has already visited the Vatican more often than his two predecessors combined. In addition, alongside Rachel, the ministry has for some time maintained a dedicated unit headed by an ambassador that deals with, among other things, "fundamental issues relating to religion and foreign policy.".

    Industry News: Trump threatens ban on US firms building AI data centres overseas

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Trump says he won't allow American companies to build data centres "outside" the US.
    • Donald Trump has noted he will ban US companies from building AI data centres overseas, threatening a "tremendous tax" for tech firms who do so.
    • "We're going to keep it all in this country," the US president mentioned, while providing little detail on the potential policy he said others in his cabinet were hearing about for the first time.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Trump says he won't allow American companies to build data centres "outside" the US.

    Donald Trump has noted he will ban US companies from building AI data centres overseas, threatening a "tremendous tax" for tech firms who do so.

    "We're going to keep it all in this country," the US president mentioned, while providing little detail on the potential policy he said others in his cabinet were hearing about for the first time.

    Data centres were a central matter in the midterm elections earlier in November, with many Democratic candidates promising tougher regulation on their construction.

    Tech giants including Meta and Google have entered agreements to build data centres overseas. It remains unclear how such a policy would be enforced if it was brought in.

    "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centres outside of our country," Trump told reporters in a press briefing following his return from his trip to Asia.

    "Because China will take all of them, and we're not allowing that to happen.".

    But whether that idea will become policy remains unclear.

    "I don't know if that's a breaking story, but I haven't even stated that to my people. But I'm telling them now, they're here," he said.

    Trump floated the policy after saying the US was leading on data centre construction, and he would not allow China to beat the US when it came to AI - which he calls super intelligence, or SI.

    It also follows an announcement earlier this week that would restrict the export of advanced computer chips and who can access the computing power provided by them.

    Washington on Monday announced firms would require a licence to buy advanced chips, so US officials can monitor whether they are being used to serve Chinese companies or they are being smuggled into China.

    The move will impact South East Asian countries that have invested heavily in data centres, as Chinese companies seek to rent computing power from overseas.

    Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back.

    Data centres are crucial to the AI boom. The vast warehouse-style buildings house the advanced computer chips and servers that are needed to run AI programmes such as Claude and ChatGPT.

    As of April there were about 3,000 data centres across the US, with another 1,500 in various stages of approval and construction, according to the Pew Research Centre.

    Many of them are built in rural areas, and concerns about problems including noise pollution and energy consumption helped drive Democratic candidates promising tougher rules on data centre construction to wins on 3 November.

    "You ought to take advantage of the data centres. Make them pay you, make them pay your community, but take advantage don't shut them off," Trump said.

    According to recent reports, "We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they're great places. They have energy and they have everything. They're tremendous assets.".

    Large tech firms - often called AI hyperscalers due to the size of their investments in AI - have also been branching out, and Canada has made moves to step in to offer itself as an alternative location for these sites, with less local pushback against projects so far.

    Meta has already broken ground on a data centre, external in the province of Alberta, and Anthropic has signed a long-term agreement to lease a proposed data centre in Nova Scotia.

    The BBC has reached out to Meta for comment on Trump's remarks.

    In September Google declared a â¬13bn ($15bn: Â£11bn) investment in AI infrastructure in Finland, which included funding for three data centres.

    Last month, building work for two of those centres was halted due to concerns over the clearance of more than 300 hectares of forest.

    Trump called out the build in Finland specifically, saying his administration was "not allowing that to happen".

    Google has been contacted for comment.

    #35884. Industry News: Setting up an Apple HomeView is ridiculously easy thanks to your iPhone

    Industry News: Setting up an Apple HomeView is ridiculously easy thanks to your iPhone

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1074 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • You can also easily add other users to your HomeView display.
    • Apple HomeView has arrived, and to set up the smart display, you'll have to use your iPhone or iPad.
    • Some of those apps are part of Apple's own core suite, including Calendar, Messages, Reminders and Weather.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    You can also easily add other users to your HomeView display.

    Apple HomeView has arrived, and to set up the smart display, you'll have to use your iPhone or iPad. Unlike other companies' smart displays, the HomeView doesn't run its own apps; it merely mirrors the compatible ones you have on your phone or tablet. It's similar to CarPlay in that regard.

    Some of those apps are part of Apple's own core suite, including Calendar, Messages, Reminders and Weather. However, the HomeView will not actually host or have access to your personal information. It will only show things like texts and calendar reminders if it can verify your identity through your face and if your paired iPhone or iPad is nearby. The idea is for all members of your household to be able to use the HomeView without compromising anybody's privacy.

    Recent findings suggest that the good news is that pairing it with an iPhone or an iPad is fairly easy. To start with, your iPhone must be running the recently released iOS 27.2, while your iPad must be running iPadOS 27.2. In addition, to be able to make the most of HomeView, you'll have to be comfortable running Apple Intelligence. It's always listening to your Siri queries, and you'll need to use Siri AI, the next-generation version of the assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, to get more useful and conversational responses.

    According to recent reports, the process of pairing and iPhone or iPad to a HomeView device is simple. You just have to hold your phone or tablet near the smart display that's powered on. You'll then see a card pop up, similar to a fresh set of AirPods or other Apple devices. If you're not running the latest iOS or iPadOS software, you'll be prompted to patch. Follow the on-screen directions (more on those below) and you're good to go.

    If you don't see a card, or if you close it accidentally, there is a more manual setup method for the HomeView. After you upgrade your operating system, open the Home app on your phone or tablet. If you've never used it before, you have to set up a new Home. Tap the + icon at the top-right corner of the screen, then Add New Home and give it a name. You will automatically be listed as the Home's Resident (Owner). If you already have a Home set up, tap the ellipsis icon at the top right, choose a Home and make sure you're its Resident (Owner).

    Next, open the Find My app and then make sure Shared From is set to This iPhone or This iPad. If it's not set to that option, and you see Use This [device] as My Location, tap it. Check that your phone's Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are switched on. If you haven't powered on your HomeView yet, do it now. Unlock your iPhone or iPad and place it near the HomeView to see a Set Up screen appear on your device.

    Now, it's time to pair your devices. You'll see a prompt on your iPhone or iPad, asking you to Center HomeView in the camera frame to capture the animation on the bigger screen. You can also tap on Enter Passcode Manually to get HomeView to show you a four-digit passcode instead. After the frame in the setup screen turns green, the process begins.

    Industry observers note that you will be asked which Home to add the HomeView to. After you've chosen, you'll get to the Where will you use this HomeView screen, where you'll have to choose the room where you want to add it to. Take note that you may be asked to update the HomeView software. After the update is done, you'll go through more prompts, including one that asks if you want your HomeView to match your iPhone settings, like your Wi-Fi network and Siri voice. Another prompt asks if you want the HomeView to be able to show personal content like messages. Once you're done, the display will show an animation while it's undergoing configuration.

    According to recent reports, from here, the setup process will move to the HomeView itself. You'll be asked to set up Face and Voice Recognition for a more personalized experience. Remember that you can't display messages and other personal information on the HomeView without authenticating your identity. Tap Continue and follow the instructions.

    According to recent reports, to set up Voice Recognition, you'll have to read several prompts shown on screen out loud. Next, you'll be able to set Facial Recognition by positioning your face in the center of the camera frame and moving it, according to the instructions on screen. This process is similar to setting up Face ID on other Apple devices. The HomeView will then show you a short tutorial of its features. The moment the Welcome screen appears, you know you're done.

    Sources indicate that apple's HomeView supports up to six people on a single device, and you — or the user listed as Resident (Owner) of the Home it has been linked to — can add them after setup is done. Open the Home app and choose the Home linked to your device. Tap the + icon and choose Add People. When asked to choose their Role, choose Resident so they can access the HomeView anytime. You will then be asked to enter their Apple/iCloud account contact and then send them an invite. They can accept the invitation in the More section that reveals up when you tap the ellipsis icon at the top right corner of the Home app.

    Industry observers note that after a user has been added, they can swipe up on the HomeView to access the Home Screen and then tap the profile icon at the top right to choose their account. Once the user brings their iPhone or iPad near the HomeView, a prompt with a Join button appear on their device. They will also have to go through several prompts, including the one asking them if they want the display to match their iPhone settings and whether they want it to show any personal information. They will then officially be added as a user and will be able to set up Voice and Facial Recognition. One user only has to swipe down the Home Screen to exit, and another user can take over once they step in front of the HomeView.

    #35882. Latest Update: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1321 w)

    Latest Update: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1321 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion.
    • Sources indicate that in a latest Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025.
    • Sources indicate that some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act.

    Sources indicate that in a latest Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar stated. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it’s really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.”.

    Sources indicate that some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges.

    Recent findings suggest that karambelkar’s team spotted a candidate system where this might be happening while searching Andromeda for stars changing in brightness, using the Wide-field Infrared Transient Explorer (WINTER) telescope at Palomar Observatory and data from NASA’s Near-Earth Object Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (NEOWISE) mission. One giant had been brightening for seven years. “When a star first swallows its companion, it has a very subtle effect on its brightness,” Karambelkar stated. “It slowly brightens, and a lot of light comes out in the infrared.”.

    Sources indicate that in April 2025, Karambelkar’s team published a paper suggesting that this system, named AT 2025abao, was undergoing an engulfment in progress. Back then, though, they couldn’t rule out a competing explanation: a single star with instabilities deep within its core. So, they kept watching.

    Industry observers note that the researchers reconstructed the history of the system using observations from about a dozen telescopes and surveys, going back to photographic sky plates from 1989. Until 2018, the star barely changed. Modeling those quiet years revealed a giant late in its life, about 350 times wider than the Sun. Its companion was impossible to see, however. “The giant star outshines the smaller star by a factor of about 18,000,” Karambelkar mentioned.

    Recent findings suggest that to get around it, the team estimated the mass of the smaller companion based on the amount of dust the system had shed before the engulfment. The estimates suggested a star of roughly 0.7 solar masses.

    In a recent development, between 2018 and early 2025, the giant brightened two- to threefold in visible light, swelling while its temperature stayed nearly constant. Karambelkar compares the process to a spacecraft reentering Earth’s atmosphere. The companion, skimming through the giant’s outer layers, was gradually seeing its orbit shrink, and the friction was heating up the envelope. The energy released by that drag matched the extra light the team observed.

    In a recent development, then, the star’s visible light dropped by half while its infrared glow kept rising. NASA’s SPHEREx space telescope happened to catch it in July 2025, revealing that the giant had swollen to some 860 times the Sun’s width and wrapped itself in fresh dust.

    It has been revealed that in October 2025, the star brightened roughly 100-fold in just 25 days, shining like 1.5 million Suns at its peak. “At one point, the rate at which the orbit was decaying became very, very fast,” Karambelkar said, comparing the release of the gravitational energy to an explosion. “The companion just fell very quickly, very deep inside the envelope of the star, and it crashed into the core. That violent crash set off a bomb inside the star, and that explosion caused it to brighten very quickly and eject some of the material.”.

    Industry observers note that the eruption had all the hallmarks of a luminous red nova, a type of outburst known to come from merging stars—but an event the researchers weren’t expecting. “Honestly, our minds were blown,” Karambelkar said. He said that this was evidence that this explosion was a consequence of the inspiraling of a binary companion. What made AT 2025abao special, though, was the giant itself.

    It has been revealed that all previously known luminous red novae came from younger stars with dense, tightly bound outer layers, which inevitably drive both stars toward a merger. This one was an old giant with a loose, churning envelope—the setup that can also leave behind a surviving tight binary. To find out if the companion actually survived, the team looked at how AT 2025abao’s energy was spent.

    To predict how such events end, astronomers use a formula with an efficiency parameter describing how much of the energy lost by the sinking companion goes into blowing the envelope away. AT 2025abao indicated that the energy goes to different places at different stages.

    According to recent reports, during the slow spiral, most of the energy escaped as light. In the final plunge, the companion released about a hundred times more energy, but only around 1 percent of it was radiated away. Nearly all the rest went into hurling a tenth of the envelope outward at about 10 times the speed needed to escape the giant’s gravity. The rest of the envelope stayed put, which suggests the companion merged with the giant’s core instead of surviving as a tight partner.

    In a recent development, “Initially, when the rate of energy deposition is low, the star is able to puff up and adjust to this newly introduced energy source inside it,” Karambelkar stated. “But once the energy deposition rate increases very quickly as the companion spirals even closer, the star can no longer adjust itself. At that point, it needs to throw out some of its material.”.

    Industry observers note that the efficiency the team calculated fits values inferred from known post-engulfment binaries. But the formula assumes the energy is mostly spent expelling lots of the envelope. Here, most of it went into flinging a small amount of gas at high speeds. It turned out the formula works as a rule of thumb but misses some of the physics.

    Industry observers note that in AT 2025abao, gas shed during the slow spiral piled up in the plane of the binary’s orbit, so the explosion’s ejecta could expand freely toward the poles even though it was blocked around the equator. That, Karambelkar argues, explains the hourglass-shaped nebulae seen around dying stars. “It had been an idea for a very long time that those hourglass shapes are shaped by binary interactions,” he said. “It seems like what we’re seeing here confirms that hypothesis.”.

    The team admits it can’t yet be sure the stars merged, because dust formed from the ejected material hides whatever is left inside. “We want to continue monitoring the system for several years, possibly even decades, to watch the dust clear out and whatever is remaining inside emerge,” Karambelkar stated. “That will conclusively tell us whether this merged or the binary system survived.” In the meantime, the team hopes to find many more such events involving stars of different masses and types.

    Telescopes we have today can detect them only as far as Andromeda, but the Vera Rubin Observatory and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope should spot them in about 100 Milky Way-like galaxies within some 50 million light-years. “We can have an influx of several of these events per year,” Karambelkar mentioned.

    Sources indicate that nature, 2026. DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11221-z.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that california’s Attorney General Rob Bonta on Thursday evening said the state has served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia following news of former CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman who the U.S.
    • The state is investigating the company to find out if its advanced GPUs or confidential information may have been shared with China, and if the company had somehow misled its investors and the public.
    • “The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the tech giant may have misled investors,” Bonta said in a statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that california’s Attorney General Rob Bonta on Thursday evening said the state has served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia following news of former CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman who the U.S. government believes is a Chinese spy.

    The state is investigating the company to find out if its advanced GPUs or confidential information may have been shared with China, and if the company had somehow misled its investors and the public.

    “The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the tech giant may have misled investors,” Bonta said in a statement.

    “My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang’s actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information — and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law,” he added.

    The investigation comes in the wake of a messy couple of weeks for Nvidia, which has overnight come under intense scrutiny around the world due to the implications of Huang’s alleged relationship with the Chinese national, Alice Huang (who is not related to Jensen).

    The Nvidia founder resigned last week after further revelations of extramarital affairs with the company’s employees. And while many tech voices have been petitioning Nvidia to bring back Huang as CEO, saying they see him as indispensable to the further development of the AI industry, the company’s newly introduced chair, Harvey Jones, said earlier this week that Nvidia had no intention of reinstating Huang to his position.

    The company’s board has hired a law firm as well as an independent slate of directors to investigate the extent of the damage, and the U.S. government is trying to find out the extent of Alice Huang’s ties with the Chinese government.

    The U.S. Congress is also gearing up to subpoena Huang, seeking questions about the affair, and the SEC is remarked to be launching a civil probe into the organization, trying to find out if Nvidia’s public disclosures could have misled investors.

    Sources indicate that democratic representatives have also opened an inquiry into the Trump administration’s management of Nvidia’s chip sales to China. In a scathing letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Democrats last week asked the Commerce Department to preserve records about an arrangement that they called questionable and illegal.

    “Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors,” Bonta wrote.

    Huang has agreed to testify before Congress after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.
